explainer.title: Understanding environmental data
explainer.description: Learn about the indicators used by CTRLCLIMA and understand what each one reveals about a region's environmental conditions.

airTemperature.title: Air temperature
airTemperature.description: Represents air temperature measured approximately 2 meters above the Earth's surface. It is expressed in degrees Celsius.

maximumTemperature.title: Maximum temperature
maximumTemperature.description: Indicates the highest air temperature recorded during each day, measured at a height of 2 meters.

minimumTemperature.title: Minimum temperature
minimumTemperature.description: Indicates the lowest air temperature recorded during each day, measured at a height of 2 meters.

precipitation.title: Precipitation
precipitation.description: Represents the estimated accumulated rainfall, expressed in millimeters per day.

humidity.title: Relative humidity
humidity.description: Indicates the amount of water vapor in the air relative to the maximum amount it could hold at that temperature.

wind.title: Wind speed
wind.description: Represents wind speed measured approximately 2 meters above the surface, generally expressed in meters per second.

difference.title: Air temperature is not surface temperature
difference.description: Air temperature, measured 2 meters above the ground, differs from land surface temperature. Asphalt, rooftops and areas without vegetation can reach surface temperatures much higher than the surrounding air. These indicators should not be interpreted as the same measurement.

reportGuide.title: How to interpret the reports?
reportGuide.description: CTRLCLIMA reports organize environmental data for the selected location and period to facilitate analysis.
reportGuide.period: Shows the dates used in the query and defines the interval of the presented data.
reportGuide.location: Presents the region and geographic coordinates of the queried point.
reportGuide.indicators: Gathers information on temperature, precipitation, humidity and wind.
reportGuide.charts: Allow users to observe indicator variations and compare different periods.
reportGuide.source: Identifies NASA POWER as the source of the environmental data used.
reportGuide.export: The PDF gathers analysis information for consultation, printing or sharing.
reportGuide.note: Important: Data represents estimates and records provided by the source for the queried location and period. An observed variation alone does not prove the cause of a climate phenomenon.
